rich_description: The National Addictions Management Service (NAMS) is the Institute of Mental Health's specialist service for all forms of addiction — alcohol, drugs (legal and illegal), gambling, gaming, pornography and sex addiction — and is the right place when an addiction is hurting work, finances, relationships, or health. Treatment is multidisciplinary: a psychiatrist assesses and prescribes (including medication-assisted detox for severe alcohol or opioid dependence), a clinical psychologist runs evidence-based therapy (motivational interviewing, CBT, relapse prevention), and a medical social worker handles family ripple effects (debt counselling for gamblers, ComCare referrals, child safety if relevant). The All Addictions Helpline (6-RECOVER, 6-7326837) is the 24-hour single number for the addicted person, family members worried about a loved one, or anyone wanting to understand what to do. NAMS is open to all Singapore residents — fees follow IMH's subsidised rates with means-tested support, and MediFund covers those who cannot pay. Confidentiality is protected by law; coming to NAMS does not create a criminal record.

other_criteria: Open to anyone in Singapore with an addiction concern; foreigners pay non-subsidised rates
Concerned family member can call the helpline first, without the addicted person's consent
Voluntary treatment does not create a criminal record
Medical bills assessed for MediShield / MediSave / MediFund support

required_documents.name: NRIC / FIN / passport
required_documents.notes: For registration; helpline calls are anonymous

required_documents.name: Referral letter
required_documents.required_if: if referred by GP or polyclinic

oth_location: NAMS operates out of IMH at Buangkok Green (10 Buangkok View). The All Addictions Helpline is staffed 24/7. PLACEHOLDER — verify whether a community outreach session is run periodically at Tampines OTH or via Tampines Polyclinic.
typical_processing_time: First appointment typically within 2-4 weeks of registration; urgent cases (severe withdrawal, suicidal ideation) seen same-week.
